title: Rust harness lifecycle and output reliability
note: Paired clean native release builds, eight standard scenarios and three trials per model (288 samples). The owner approved gemini-3.8-flash-high at high effort because the gateway lacks gemini-3.8-flash-medium; standard Gemini coverage remains missing. Five models succeeded in all 24 candidate tasks. GPT failed 7 candidate and 4 base tasks: 6 versus 4 malformed streamed edit calls stopped by the existing whitespace guard, plus one candidate provider-overload response. These are retained as failures; provider stochasticity and differing executable paths prevent attributing the imbalance to this change. Sonnet added one expected failing pre-repair test and DeepSeek Flash added one failed exploratory read of an absent package.json; both tasks subsequently passed unchanged independent checks. DeepSeek Flash used 7.6% more tokens (95% interval 0.7–15.9) with five extra requests, concentrated in shell_then_edit and stale_edit. That cost increase is accepted for this security/lifecycle patch with all 24 tasks passing; no efficiency gain or proven causal attribution is claimed. The record remains regression-flagged. Deterministic fixtures separately establish output cancellation, provider idle/drop cleanup, observer isolation, and persistence ordering. JSON exit-zero after a model error was also observed in both arms and is addressed by the subsequent typed-run-outcome change, outside this measured candidate.

settings.effort: medium where the model offers it; DeepSeek runs at high, its default, having no medium

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
